titulo: Build your own: the grocery store and meu-assistente.md
lead: INTELECTO v2 is already working. The grocery store helps you choose what to add: it builds an .md file with the ingredients, each one’s status in the project, and rules for a coding agent. You can just read a ready-made example without using an agent or spending credits.
objetivo: Choose an example, interpret the .md markers, and say what already exists and what still needs to be implemented.

aprende.t: Choose ingredients or load a ready-made example
Read the total, markers, and files mentioned in the .md
Give the agent one item at a time and check the tests

hero_alt: Humanoid beside a grocery cart with blank cards pointing to a blank document.

secoes.sub: Click the three steps. The symbols show what already exists and what’s missing.
secoes.legenda: ✅ already exists in INTELECTO v2, with the file · 🟡 exists in part · ➕ needs to be added, with the part to add it to.

nos.detalhe: At the grocery store, choose from eight aisles or load one of the five ready-made examples. There are 144 ingredients from 12 agent projects.
Open the cart and click Export. The meu-assistente.md file classifies each item: ✅ with a file, 🟡 partial, ➕ with the part where it fits.
Copy the .md to INTELECTO and ask Claude Code or Codex to implement one partial or added item at a time. Check the code and tests before moving on.

secoes.sub: The page builds a work list; it doesn’t install features.

texto: Personal Jarvis on Telegram: 12 items (✅ 5, 🟡 3, ➕ 4). Small business assistant: 12 (✅ 2, 🟡 2, ➕ 8). Secure programmer: 12 (✅ 4, 🟡 0, ➕ 8).
100% local and private: 10 items (✅ 5, 🟡 1, ➕ 4). Voice-controlled smart home: 12 (✅ 2, 🟡 0, ➕ 10). All five files are in the repository’s exemplos/ folder.
✅ already exists and names the actual file, such as intelecto/canais/telegram.py; 🟡 exists in part and says what’s missing; ➕ doesn’t exist yet and points to the part where the agent can add code.

The .md says to work on one ingredient at a time, write a test in tests/ and run python3 -m pytest -q. It also says to preserve the lock, keep secrets only in the vault, test without a real API, update the process table in README when usage changes, and say “done” only with the test output.

secoes.titulo: Open an example and hand off the plan
secoes.sub: The first try only reads the file and doesn’t use an agent. The second is optional and uses your agent subscription or credits.

blocos.rot: Terminal · read the example for free
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/intelecto-v2
less exemplos/01-jarvis-telegram.md
# Press q to exit less.

blocos.rot: Terminal · copy the example to the project
With Claude Code or Codex open in the folder
blocos.conteudo: Read meu-assistente.md and implement the items to add and the partial items, one at a time, following the Rules for the agent.

blocos.rot: Terminal · count tests before and after an item
blocos.conteudo:
sudo apt install -y python3-pytest   # the test program (just once)
cd ~/intelecto-v2
python3 -m pytest -q

blocos.rot: Optional practice · request for ONE ➕ item
blocos.conteudo: Read meu-assistente.md. Choose only ONE item marked ➕, implement it, write the test in tests/ and run python3 -m pytest -q. Show the changed code and the test output.

paragrafos: The grocery store creates the plan in Markdown. The coding agent writes the code for 🟡 and ➕ items; you need to check its work. This uses your agent subscription or credits. Safer option: run the agent in caixa-do-agente and apply only the reviewed patch to the original.
For a file downloaded from the grocery store, copy ~/Downloads/meu-assistente.md to ~/intelecto-v2/. If you use the repository example, the block above copies it without a download.

secoes.sub: The first practice doesn’t need an agent, Docker, or payment.

exercicios.texto: Open exemplos/01-jarvis-telegram.md in the repository or download an example from the shop. Find the “Total: …” line and a ✅ item with a file path. In Jarvis, use the Telegram bot as an example.
exercicios.pronto: You can say: 12 items; ✅ 5, 🟡 3, and ➕ 4; and name the file for one ✅ item, for example intelecto/canais/telegram.py.

exercicios.texto: Install the test program once (sudo apt install -y python3-pytest). Copy meu-assistente.md to ~/intelecto-v2, run python3 -m pytest -q, and note how many tests pass. Give the agent just ONE ➕ item, following the file’s rules. The agent writes the code; check the patch or changes and run the tests again. This uses your subscription or the agent’s credits.
exercicios.pronto: python3 -m pytest -q passes after the change and shows more passing tests than before. You checked the code the agent produced.

secoes.sub: Answer based on the diagram and example file.

perguntas.p: What does ➕ mean on an item in meu-assistente.md?
opcoes: Already exists and points to the file
perguntas.explica: ➕ marks something to add; the file shows where it fits. ✅ cites existing code, and 🟡 shows what exists in part.

perguntas.p: Why implement one item at a time and test before moving to the next?
opcoes: To know which change passed and fix failures before moving on
So the agent doesn’t have to read the file’s rules
To replace the tests with a well-written answer
perguntas.explica: The .md rules ask for one ingredient at a time, tests in tests/, and a green python3 -m pytest -q before moving on.

perguntas.p: Where can you find the code for a ✅ item?
opcoes: At the file path cited by the item itself
Only in the image of the finished example
In the browser cart after exporting
perguntas.explica: The ✅ item cites the INTELECTO file that already implements the function, such as intelecto/canais/telegram.py.

itens.texto: The shop exports meu-assistente.md with choices and markers; the file doesn’t install anything.
The agent implements 🟡 and ➕; you check the changes and require passing tests before continuing.
